body: You book it here. An email follows with instructions for choosing a time that suits you. At the time you chose, the call happens, and it runs for an hour.
Bring your questions written down. An hour goes quickly, and most people spend the first ten minutes remembering what they meant to ask.
It is not a medical appointment. Nothing said in the hour is a diagnosis, a prescription, or a reason to stop or change anything you have been prescribed.
If you take prescribed medication, your GP and your pharmacist are the two people who can check anything against it. If what you need is urgent, ring 111 or your surgery rather than booking an hour.
Whether the call is recorded, whether you are sent notes afterwards, what happens if you need to move the time, how far ahead the diary runs, and what the letters after the name stand for.
None of that is on the listing, so none of it is promised here. Ring the shop and ask before you book if any of it decides the matter for you.
On a private audio call, not in the shop. The listing does not name the platform it is made on or say who rings whom.
If you would rather ask at a counter, the shop is at 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, open 10 to 6, any day except Monday.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The listing for this hour is written almost entirely in outcomes: what you will gain, what you will come away with, what will be tailored to you. None of that is on this page, because an outcome sold in advance is a promise, and an hour of conversation cannot carry one. What is here is the length, the price, the way it is arranged and the rows the listing leaves empty.

reiss.label: From Reiss
reiss.h2: What an hour is, and is not
paras: An hour on the phone is an hour of questions answered by somebody who reads labels for a living and has spent a long time behind a counter. It is not an appointment, I am not your doctor, and if what you actually need is a diagnosis then this is the wrong thing to buy and I will tell you so in the first five minutes rather than the last.

The listing sets out at length what you are meant to get out of it. That part is not on this page. What is here is how long it lasts, what it costs, how it is arranged, and the things nobody has written down yet, such as whether you get notes afterwards and what happens if you have to move the time.
reiss.pull: I am not your doctor. If what you need is a diagnosis, this is the wrong thing to buy.
